article.title: は tópico
article.part: Arquitectura básica de la oración — 文の基本構造
article.chapter: Tópico, sujeto y contraste: は/が — 主題・主語・対比：は／が

claims.summary: Yoshimoto (1982) describes thematic wa as setting a noun phrase against the discourse background and treats wa as a discourse-level theme marker, distinct from the syntactic relation of a noun phrase to its predicate.
Nose (2017) gives the Japanese examples Watashi-wa hon-o yomu and Watashi-wa kono hon-ga sukida, glossing them with wa-marked topic phrases and, in the latter, a ga-marked phrase in the comment.

locator.description: J-STAGE article overview, abstract (journal pp. 1–17): thematic wa sets an element against the discourse background; wa marks a noun phrase as a theme and belongs to discourse grammar (abstract lines 54–57).

links.notes: La afirmación describe explícitamente el análisis de Yoshimoto.

locator.description: PDF pp. 48–49, section on Japanese information structure, examples (2a–c): Watashi-wa hon-o yomu and Watashi-wa kono hon-ga sukida, with glosses identifying wa as topic and ga as subject marker.

links.notes: Los ejemplos y glosas se copiaron del estudio; la traducción española se ofrece como glosa propia.

locator.description: J-STAGE abstract, article overview, lines 54–57: wa can occur outside nominative marking, while ga relates an NP to its predicate.

links.notes: Respalda la distinción funcional que contextualiza los ejemplos.
